title: 3 charts on the tokenized stocks boom - a16z crypto
gist: Tokenized stocks grew from $329M to $1.7B market cap in a year (5x) with a 170x jump in monthly transfer volume, and the growth is driven by new issuance rather than price appreciation, while composition shifted sharply away from crypto-linked names toward AI/chips, megacap tech, and ETFs as DTCC, Robinhood, NYSE, Coinbase, and Binance all launched infrastructure in the past month.

themes.theme: Tokenized stocks market growth is issuance-driven, not just repricing

insights.claim: The market cap of tokenized stocks reached about $1.7 billion at the end of June 2026, up from $329 million a year earlier, more than 5x growth, making it one of the fastest-growing categories of tokenized real-world assets.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: Tracks the pace at which equities are moving onchain; a 5x annual growth rate signals an accelerating category worth monitoring for platform and infrastructure plays.
insights.quote: The market cap of tokenized stocks reached about $1.7 billion at the end of June, up from $329 million a year earlier — more than 5x growth.
insights.locator: The momentum shows up in the data

insights.claim: More than half of the current tokenized-stocks market cap sits in assets that were not onchain a year ago, and most of the remaining balance arrived mid-year after most of the underlying stocks' price movement had already occurred, indicating the growth is driven by new issuance rather than price appreciation.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: New issuance rather than price appreciation implies the category's growth is structural (more assets being tokenized) rather than a market-driven artifact, a more durable signal for adoption.
insights.quote: The evidence points to issuance though. More than half of today’s market cap sits in assets that weren’t onchain a year ago.
insights.locator: How much of that growth comes from new issuance

insights.claim: Monthly transfer volume for tokenized stocks reached $9.22 billion in June 2026, up from $53 million a year earlier, a more than 170x increase, measuring onchain trading, wallet transfers, and DeFi collateral deposits.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: Transfer volume growing far faster than market cap (170x vs 5x) suggests utility and active usage (trading, collateral) are scaling even faster than the asset base itself.
insights.quote: Monthly transfer volume for tokenized stocks reached $9.22 billion in June, up from $53 million last June — a more than 170x increase.
insights.locator: Transfer activity is on the rise too

themes.theme: Category composition shifted away from crypto-linked names toward AI/chips, megacap tech, and ETFs

insights.claim: Crypto-linked tokenized products' share of the tokenized-stocks market by market cap dropped to 21% in June 2026 from 79% a year earlier, losing the top spot to a long tail of "other" listings.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: The category is diversifying beyond crypto-native tickers, suggesting broader institutional and retail equity tokenization rather than a crypto-only niche.
insights.quote: Crypto-linked products once dominated the market, but their share by market cap has dropped to 21% (as of June) from 79% a year earlier.
insights.locator: While the market for tokenized stocks is new

insights.claim: The "other" category, a long tail of hundreds of smaller listings, grew to 35% of the tokenized-stocks market by June 2026, up from 15% a year earlier, and is now the largest segment.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: A long tail becoming the plurality segment points to broad-based, fragmented issuance rather than concentration in a few flagship tokenized names.
insights.quote: They have lost the top spot to the “other” category — a long tail of hundreds of smaller listings — that now makes up 35% of the market, up from 15% a year earlier.
insights.locator: While the market for tokenized stocks is new

insights.claim: The AI and chips category was the fastest riser in tokenized stocks, growing from less than $1 million (0.3% of market cap) in June 2025 to 15.5% of the market by June 2026.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: AI/chips names are being tokenized and traded onchain at the fastest rate of any segment, signaling strong demand for exposure to that theme via tokenized wrappers.
insights.quote: The fastest riser has been, unsurprisingly, the AI and chips category. The category vaulted from less than $1 million in June 2025 — 0.3% of the market by market cap at the time — to 15.5% of the market as of a year later.

insights.claim: Megacap tech companies (roughly $100 billion+ market cap) grew to 10.6% of the tokenized-stocks market by June 2026, up from 0.6% a year earlier, while ETFs and indices grew to 17.3% from 4.5% over the same period.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: Both megacap tech and passive ETF/index exposure are being tokenized at a fast clip, suggesting tokenization is spreading into mainstream, widely-held equity products, not just niche assets.
insights.quote: Megacap tech — tech companies with a market cap around $100 billion or more — now make up 10.6% of the market by market cap as of June, up from 0.6% a year ago.
insights.locator: The rest of the market is climbing too

themes.theme: Institutional infrastructure for tokenized equities is being built out rapidly

insights.claim: In the past month, DTCC processed its first live production trades of tokenized Treasuries and equities on Digital Asset's Canton Network, with a full launch of the broader tokenization service planned for October, giving Wall Street a direct on-ramp to roughly $114 trillion in assets custodied at DTC.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: DTCC's move signals mainstream custodial infrastructure is preparing to connect one of the largest pools of traditional securities (~$114T) to onchain rails, a major scaling catalyst if the October launch proceeds.
insights.quote: DTCC processed its first live production trades of tokenized Treasuries and equities on Digital Asset’s Canton Network. (A full launch of the broader tokenization service is planned for October, giving Wall Street a direct on-ramp to the ~$114T in assets custodied at DTC.)
insights.locator: The institutional groundwork is now falling into place

insights.claim: In the past month, Robinhood launched its own blockchain on mainnet to bring traditional markets, crypto, and real-world assets together on an open network; the NYSE's parent company announced a joint venture with OKX (June 22) to make tokenized NYSE-listed stocks available pending regulatory approval; Coinbase said it will offer 1:1-backed tokenized U.S. stocks to non-U.S. users with dividends and full shareholder rights (June 16); and Binance shipped a similar product days earlier.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: A cluster of major exchanges and brokers (Robinhood, NYSE/OKX, Coinbase, Binance) launching tokenized-equity products within weeks of each other suggests competitive pressure is accelerating institutional adoption, worth tracking for platform-share dynamics.
insights.quote: Robinhood launched its own chain on mainnet... the parent company of the NYSE announced a joint venture with OKX to make tokenized NYSE-listed stocks available to users, pending regulatory approval... Coinbase said it will offer 1:1-backed tokenized U.S. stocks to non-U.S. users, with dividends, full shareholder rights, and 24/7 trading. Binance shipped its own version days before.
